subject.title: fix(agents): dripping proxy SSE streams hang past chunk-idle timeout

question: Should proxied SSE model responses have an unconditional one-hour maximum lifetime, or should total lifetime remain owned exclusively by the configured agent/provider abort budget?
rationale: Both policies are defensible, but the patch changes valid long-stream behavior below currently supported outer budgets and no existing documented contract selects one hour.

options.title: Use outer configured budget
options.body: Remove the fixed one-hour default and prove the existing run/provider abort signal cancels dripping proxy bodies while retaining chunk-idle detection.

options.title: Adopt one-hour cap
options.body: Explicitly approve and document the one-hour fail-closed policy, align it with timeout configuration, and prove fresh and upgrade behavior for long streams.

options.title: Pause this cutoff
options.body: Keep current behavior until a concrete production reproduction shows the outer runtime deadline does not terminate the proxy stream.

recommendation.title: Use outer configured budget
recommendation.body: Remove the fixed one-hour default and prove the existing run/provider abort signal cancels dripping proxy bodies while retaining chunk-idle detection.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent adjacent agent timeout and abort-propagation work makes this the strongest available owner for choosing the canonical lifetime boundary.
